quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The center of the lane
The right side of the lane
It depends on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Choose a position that fits your current conditions. Make sure you have enough space around you and that other drivers can see you.

questions.question: Which color vest or jacket helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. Bright red, orange, yellow, or green work best. Avoid dark or dull colors.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep using the rear brake.
Swerve toward the safest area.
Speed up while braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Release the brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. On dry pavement, you can keep the brake locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When shifting into neutral
When you are about to slow down quickly
When you see a stop sign ahead
When your turn signals are broken

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are about to slow down quickly
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down suddenly, especially if a vehicle is following too closely. This gives the driver behind you a warning about hazards ahead.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit
Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes
Shift into neutral when slowing down
Speed up before turning

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands near the clutch and brakes
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area like an intersection, position your hands near the clutch and both brakes. This lets you react faster if a hazard appears.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Slow down
Avoid sudden movements
Use only the front brake when stopping
Use both brakes when stopping

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when stopping
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oil, dirt, gravel, shade, and bridges—these are more slippery.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear
Apply the rear brake first, then the front
Use both brakes at the same time
Use the brakes in any order

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.

options.text: Farther away, more slowly
Farther away, faster
Closer, more slowly
Closer, faster

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away, more slowly
questions.explanation: Motorcycles and small vehicles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their real location and speed.

questions.question: If you must brake while turning, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more slowly than on a straight road
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road
Wait until the curve is over to brake
Use only the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more slowly than on a straight road
questions.explanation: When leaning in a curve, your tires have less grip. If you must brake while turning, apply brakes gently and smoothly. It is best to straighten up before braking.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is ______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.

options.text: Two times
Three times
Six times
20 times

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times
questions.explanation: Riders who wear helmets are three times more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so other drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb. Touch your rear wheel to the curb.

questions.question: What do rounded, convex mirrors on motorcycles do?

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars seem closer than they actually are.
Show only a narrow view of the road.
Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They make objects behind you look farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to them.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease your following distance.
Use the headlights of the vehicle in front of you to see ahead.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of the vehicle in front of you to see ahead.
questions.explanation: To prevent collisions at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position at any time.

questions.question: What should you do if a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your lane.
questions.explanation: Avoid hitting animals when you can, but stay in your lane when riding in traffic. Swerving into another lane to miss a small animal could cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting a car.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop far back, then slowly move forward.
Stay well behind the vehicle.
Make a quick stop right behind it.
Stay about four car lengths behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay well behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay a good distance behind the vehicle in front of you, even when both of you are stopped. The vehicle could back up, or you may need space to move away from a vehicle coming up behind you.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time. This is especially helpful in areas where hazards might appear.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a single-file formation.
In a side-by-side formation.
Using both lanes if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, entering highways, or leaving highways. Use staggered formation at other times.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Slow down before turning.
Lean in the direction you want to turn.
Do not drag your feet on the road.
Avoid looking at other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid looking at other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Keep your feet up and off the road. Always watch for other vehicles on the road.

questions.question: When someone is passing you from behind, where should you stay in your lane?

options.text: In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.
Activate your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic. Staying closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time and brake harder.
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.
Do neither action.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. You need good traction to swerve safely. Instead, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: As a rider, what should you NOT tell a passenger to do before they ride?

options.text: Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Stay far away from you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from you.
questions.explanation: Passengers should get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you. They should hold onto the handholds or your waist, hips, or belt—not stay far away. They must keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should riders do?

options.text: Spread out so others can see the group better.
Stay close together so others can see the group better.
Separate from time to time.
Ride in pairs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay close together so others can see the group better.
questions.explanation: Riders should stay close together while keeping safe space around each motorcycle. This makes the group easier to see and keeps riders from getting separated. Pairs do not give enough room to maneuver.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What must an eye or face shield do to work well?

options.text: Fasten securely.
Stop all air from passing through.
Not allow eyeglasses underneath.
Limit your side vision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must be scratch-free, resist breaks, allow clear side views, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes.
Press hard on the front brake to stop the front tire from locking.
Use only the rear brake.
Use one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel and use gentle pressure on the rear brake.
